name: roof-above
notes: Roof from ABOVE (the machine on top of the roof, in open air). Roof slab y 3..5 solid bedrock; target T [0,5,0] (top layer, bedrock on every side). A = swap piston [0,6,0] on top of T, facing WEST (head [-1,6,0]), retracted at rest. Its only power is quasi-connectivity through X [1,7,0] (a stone beside the cell above A), strongly powered from above by observer O [1,8,0] facing up (it watches [1,9,0], its output face points down into X). O switches with flags 2 and updates only X and X's neighbours, never A: A's power comes and goes silently. U [0,6,3] (sticky, facing north, extended, holding a stone at [0,6,1] beside A). Per cycle: [1,9,0] changes; 2 ticks later O turns ON; in that tick U's pull (its power removed just before) takes the stone away from [0,6,1] in the block-event phase and that update finds A powered: A extends. 2 ticks later O turns OFF (silent) and A's own head LANDS in the block-entity phase: the landing forwards an update to A, which finds it extended and unpowered: retract queued after that tick's block events = ARMED for the next window. The player's press there (break A, place a piston facing DOWN, i.e. looking up: crawling beside it) leaves a piston whose queued retract runs unpowered and removes T. Unswapped, A just retracts; U pushes its stone back and the next trigger repeats.
